text:
sara: NovaHealth just opened an escalation — they see 503s and 500s for hosted inference across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. customer on call, high traffic, pretty upset. sending logs now.
kevin: grabbing the trace. any indication if this is auth or upstream worker crashes?
lee: I see repeated worker restarts in the upstream pool, restart_count increments rapidly. suspect OOM/segfault.
oncall-bot: alert: novahealth-prod: 503-rate > 15% for 2m, routed to #incidents.
maria: pasted recent logs: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:14:02Z] runner[pid=2345]: ATTENTION_KERNEL: invalid read at 0x7ff... in attn_kernel.cu:174
[2026-03-17T12:14:02Z] runtime: GPU OOM allocating 12.3G for kv_cache
[2026-03-17T12:14:03Z] containerd: container exited with status 137
[2026-03-17T12:14:04Z] watcher: restart_count=6, last_exit=SIGSEGV
```
kevin: that looks like a GPU OOM immediately followed by a SIGSEGV in the attention kernel — likely memory corruption after an OOM path. which model and config?
lee: model is open-llama-70b-quant-swap:v2 with tool-calling enabled for NovaHealth chatflow. context lengths were ~64k tokens on some requests.
sara: customer says they hit the problem when calling our streaming API with a long system prompt + tool call. payload sample (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-70b-quant-swap:v2","input":"<~64k tokens>","stream":true,"tool_calls":[...]}'
```
alex_ops: kube events show node gpu memory pressure around the same time, plus eviction events. kubelet OOM killer triggered containerd.
eng-runtime: interesting — we pushed a quantization swap last night to improve cost, v2 changed KV cache layout. not seeing this in canaries. maybe edge case with long contexts + tool metadata.
maria: attaching internal artifact: s3://redwood-collects/novahealth/4487654321/hosted-runner-stdout.log (link) 
support-bot: notif sent to novahealth: "we're investigating, temporary workaround: reduce context length or pin to earlier model version."
kevin: repro steps I'm running: repeated curl with 64k context, qps=10, after ~30s worker mem climbs then container exits with 137. collecting coredump now.
lee: can you paste the nvml logs and python backtrace from the runtime? the segfault line points to the fused_attn kernel.
kevin: nvml shows GPU memory spike to 99%, then our runtime attempts to allocate additional 12GB and fails. backtrace: 
```
#0  0x7f8a1a2d in fused_attn_forward(...) at attn_kernel.cu:174
#1  0x7f8a2b3f in forward_loop at runtime/forward.cc:1023
#2  0x7f8a3c7a in main_loop at runtime/daemon.cc:451
```
maria: confirmed restart pattern across 6 different pods in two AZs — not isolated to single host.
eng-runtime: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback quant-swap to v1.3.2 (less aggressive KV layout), 2) temporarily route NovaHealth traffic to a warm dedicated pool with larger GPU memory, 3) apply request-level rejection for >32k tokens.
alex_ops: I can failover their route to the dedicated warmpool now (low risk). which option do we want?
sara: do failover + rollback. inform CS and customer. we need a postmortem if rollback is root cause.
kevin: rolling back model variant on the hosted pool for novahealth route now -> applying policy: route->dedicated-warmpool-1; updating routing rules.
eng-runtime: starting rollback of quant-swap on the upstream fleet (deploy: v1.3.2) — will monitor.
oncall-bot: deployment started: eng-runtime/quant-swap-rollback @ 2026-03-17T12:32:00Z
lee: after switching route, latency and error rate drop to normal for NovaHealth in us-west-2. watching eu-west-1.
maria: coredump uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/coredumps/4487654321/core. attaching ticket with kernel traceback to the internal bug.
sara: customer update sent: "We've routed your traffic to a dedicated warm pool and reverted a recent quantization swap. We're monitoring and will follow up."
kevin: next steps for eng-runtime: (a) reproduce locally with same long context, (b) add stronger OOM handling path so we don't hit SIGSEGV after allocation failure, (c) add autoscale rules to warmpool for sudden context spikes.
eng-runtime: agree. we'll add a runtime guard that checks for memory reservation failure and falls back to safe codepath instead of continuing into fused kernel.
lee: triage notes: possible root cause = quant-swap produced kv cache pointer arithmetic that doesn't handle near-OOM paths with extremely long context + tool metadata. need unit test for >50k tokens and tool-calling.
alex_ops: opened incident ticket INC-2026-4487654321 and scheduled 2hr postmortem slot.
sara: thanks team. leaving this thread open until postmortem and customer confirm. :white_check_mark:
